request.body: Describe this photograph for a reader who cannot see it, in 2-4 plain present-tense sentences, as a witness standing where the camera stands. There is no narrator: never write "I", "me", "my", "we" or "us", and never say who took the picture or why. The reader already knows when and where the picture was taken and whose archive it belongs to; your job is only what is inside the frame. Start with what the frame is pointed at: the subject that fills or centres the picture (a person, an object, a view, a document, a meal). Some people have a box drawn around them with a name beside it; the box means that person's identity is confirmed. Use their name, spelled exactly as written, as the subject of your sentence, say briefly what they wear and what they are visibly doing, and never mention or describe the boxes, labels, or any markings on the image. Describe people without a box generically ("a woman in a red sari") and never guess their names or identities. Account for everyone visible, including small or background figures, and state the total number of people when they can be counted. Left and right mean the viewer's left and right as the picture is seen, never the subject's own left or right. Then the setting as far as it is visible: indoors or outdoors, the kind of room or street, the light, the objects around. If the picture itself shows where the camera is (an arm held out for a selfie, an airplane window frame, a mirror, a screen, a hand holding something toward the lens), say so in those terms; otherwise say nothing about the camera. State only what is directly visible: do not invent moods, relationships, occasions, purposes, or place names, and do not guess the time of day, the season, or what happened before or after. Quote short visible text that matters, in its original language, but only what you can actually read: when only part of a word or phrase is visible, quote the visible part and say the rest is cut off or hidden, and never complete a word the image does not finish. If the photograph is chiefly text (a screen, document, sign, receipt or menu), say so first and quote the few words that matter. Never reproduce one-time codes, passwords, full card or account numbers, or other authentication secrets even when legible; say the kind of thing they are instead. If something important is too small or unclear to read, say that.
